title: Why conflicts happen
concept: Two edits to the same lines; cause a real conflict

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Most merges just work. Git matches up the changes by itself.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: But if two people change **the same line**, git cannot guess which one is right.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: That is a **conflict**. It is not an error and nothing is broken.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: You changed the title on your branch. Sam changed the same title on main.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Try the merge and see what git says. Causing one on purpose is the fastest way to learn.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Do not fix it yet. Next level we read it properly.

items.text: Try to merge feature into main

questions.prompt: The merge stopped. What is true right now?

choices.text: Git threw away one of the two versions
Git stopped and left both versions in the file for me to decide

questions.explanation: Git never picks a winner on its own. It pauses the merge and puts both versions in the file so a human can choose.

recap: A conflict happens when two branches change the same line. Git pauses the merge and asks you to decide. Nothing is broken and nothing is lost.

predict.question: You and Sam both changed the title line. What will the merge do?

choices.text: Keep Sam's version, because it is on main
Stop and ask you to decide

predict.explanation: Git will not choose for you when the same line changed on both sides.

hints: You are on main. Merge the other branch in and see what happens.
`git merge <branch>` joins that branch into the one you are on.
